description:
The DUPKEY half of the shared duplicate arm at app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:260-266. Lines :260 and :261 are two consecutive WHEN clauses with no statements between them - COBOL's way of writing 'either of these' - so DFHRESP(DUPKEY) and DFHRESP(DUPREC) both fall into the same four statements: MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG at :262, the 'User ID already exist...' literal into WS-MESSAGE at :263-264, MOVE -1 TO USERIDL at :265 and PERFORM SEND-USRADD-SCREEN at :266. This case takes the DUPKEY half and case09 takes the DUPREC half by colliding on the seeded id ADMIN001, so the two RESP values are shown to differ while nothing observable does. Note the cursor: :265 uses USERIDL where the WHEN OTHER arm at :272 uses FNAMEL, a difference of two lines that is easy to lose.

Why RESP 15 is forced rather than arranged. EXEC CICS WRITE at :240-248 addresses the USRSEC base KSDS, and a colliding primary key on a base cluster reports DUPREC (14), never DUPKEY (15), which CICS raises on an alternate index. No arrangement of the ten seeded rows can reach this half, so the outcome is stipulated at the repository boundary and the RESP is stated explicitly to keep the two halves distinguishable.

Blank-field chain position 3 is deliberately not this case. The five arms of the EVALUATE TRUE at :117-151 are pinned in source order by case02 through case06, so a blank USERIDI reaching :130-135 is case04. Restating it here would cover an already covered arm and leave the forced-DUPKEY half of :260 unreached.

Key width. USERIDI is PIC X(8) at app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:72 - eight, not twenty - and :154 moves it into SEC-USR-ID, declared PIC X(08) at app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:18. That is the primary key of the cluster app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:64-73 defines with KEYS(8,0) RECORDSIZE(80,80) INDEXED, and :244-245 pass it as both RIDFLD and KEYLENGTH. Here the id NEWUSR01 is eight characters and well formed; what fails is the collision, not the key.

Nothing is written. The arm raises WS-ERR-FLG at :262, so expectedWrites is empty and no add ever completes against USRSEC. expectedFinalState pins all ten seeded rows byte for byte at the copybook's eighty, and expectedDatasets pins the count at exactly ten rows of eighty bytes on the FINAL_STATE channel. Together they refuse both a mutated row and an unreported eleventh one - a count is not a substitute for reading the bytes, and reading the bytes cannot by itself say that no further row exists.

Message widths, derived rather than counted by eye. The literal at :263 is 24 characters. The MOVE into WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) at :38 space-fills it, so the WS_MESSAGE_80 channel carries 24 + 56 spaces = 80. MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :188 truncates an alphanumeric receiver on the RIGHT into PIC X(78) at app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:164, so the SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 channel carries 24 + 54 spaces = 78 and is the leading 78 characters of the 80. The two bytes dropped are spaces here, and the channels are stated separately because the widths are not interchangeable.

Record image. SEC-USER-DATA is 8 + 20 + 20 + 8 + 1 + 23 = 80 at app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23. The ten rows this case seeds are the 57 characters app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 carries in stream - id 1-8, first name 9-28, last name 29-48, password 49-56, type 57 - which is 80 less the absent SEC-USR-FILLER PIC X(23) at :23. The 57-to-80 pad is declared once in normalisations and applied by the harness at seed time, never at comparison time, so a width disagreement in a failure is always a real difference and never a missing declaration. SEC-USR-PWD stays plaintext at eight characters because :157 stores it that way; hashing it would be a behaviour change.

Styling and attributes. COUSR01C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY, and COPY DFHATTR at :57 is commented out, so no '*' marker and no per-field DFHRED exists anywhere in this program. MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC at :254 is the only attribute assignment and belongs to the NORMAL arm alone, so this send keeps the map's default colour on ERRMSGC at app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:160. INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :287-295 is performed only from :252 and :281, not from this arm, so the five typed values stay on the screen for the operator to correct.

Statelessness. EIBCALEN is non-zero and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1, so :83 takes the re-entry path to RECEIVE-USRADD-SCREEN at :89 and DFHENTER selects PROCESS-ENTER-KEY at :91-92. All sixteen CARDDEMO-COMMAREA fields travel in the request and back in the response, and nothing is held server side. :107-110 returns with TRANSID 'CU01', which is why the response names its own program, mapset and map rather than an XCTL target.

Determinism and encoding. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the instant in this program's own version footer at :298, so POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :214-233 yields CURDATEO 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO 23:12:34 with no dependence on the wall clock. Bytes are US-ASCII, named explicitly rather than left to a platform default. The titles are the literals at app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22, where the 'Credit Card Demo Application (CCDA)' line at :21 is commented out and the CardDemo line at :22 is what CCDA-TITLE02 actually carries. The dataset is addressed by the binding key USRSEC, whose DSNAME lives in app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:88-89 and in configuration, never in this fixture.

Provenance. Every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:57, :78-110, :117-160, :184-196, :214-233, :238-274 and :287-298, cross-checked against app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:67, :72, :146, :160 and :164, app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:88-89 and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 and :64-73. It was NOT captured from a live COBOL execution: AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers - no z/OS runtime, an indexed file handler disabled in the available compiler, subprogram linkage that cannot produce an executable, a copybook that fails to parse, no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator, EBCDIC fixtures needing binary handling the compiler is not configured for, and no alternative compiler - so the provenance is derivation from source and fixtures, carried as risk R-A rather than presented as a captured baseline.
